'''Ronald Prescott Loui''' is an American computer scientist and adjunct professor of [[computer science]] at [[Case Western Reserve University]]. He previously taught at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] and [[University of Illinois Springfield]].

==Biography==

Loui grew up in Hawaii, where he was a classmate of [[Barack Obama]] at [[Punahou School]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kaste |first=Martin |date=2012-10-12 |title=Hawaii Prep School Gave Obama Window To Success |url=https://www.npr.org/2012/10/13/162786014/hawaii-prep-school-gave-obama-window-to-success |access-date=2025-06-05 |work=NPR |language=en}}</ref><ref>Obama's link to Hawaii not ignored by islanders - The Washington Post, Apr 30, 2013</ref> He went on to earn a bachelor's degree from [[Harvard University]] in applied mathematics in 1982, where his undergraduate thesis won an ACM award.<ref>George E. Forsythe Award, 1983 shared, "Optimal paths in graphs with stochastic or multidimensional weights," CACM 26:9, 1983.</ref> He completed a Ph.D. advised by [[Henry E. Kyburg Jr.]], at the [[University of Rochester]] in 1987.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|122112}}</ref>

He was a postdoctoral researcher at [[Stanford University]] in 1987–1988, working there with [[Patrick Suppes]] and [[Amos Tversky]], among others.
From 1988 to 2008, he was a professor of computer science at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] in the [[McKelvey School of Engineering]]. He was also associated with multiple departments outside of engineering.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ronald Prescott Loui |url=https://docslib.org/ronald-prescott-loui|type=Curriculum vitae |access-date=2022-08-21 |via=Docslib |language=en}}</ref>

Loui has published papers on [[defeasible reasoning]] in [[artificial intelligence]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Loui |first=R. P. |date=1987 |title=Defeat among arguments: a system of defeasible inference |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1467-8640.1987.tb00178.x |journal=Computational Intelligence |language=en |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=100–106 |doi=10.1111/j.1467-8640.1987.tb00178.x |issn=1467-8640|url-access=subscription |hdl=1802/6395 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> and he is a proponent of [[scripting language]]s.<ref>"In Praise of Scripting," IEEE COMPUTER, 2008.</ref> He is co-patent holder of a [[deep packet inspection]] hardware device that could read and edit the contents of packets as they stream through a network.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.patentstorm.us/patents/7093023.html |title=Methods, systems, and devices using reprogrammable hardware for high-speed processing of streaming data to find a redefinable pattern and respond thereto&nbsp;– US Patent 7093023 Abstract |publisher=Patentstorm.us |accessdate=March 16, 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110612201322/http://www.patentstorm.us/patents/7093023.html |archivedate=June 12, 2011 }}</ref>
